For Respondents : Mr.M.Muthumanikkam,
 Government Advocate (Crl.Side)
 for R1  : Mrs.S.Riswana Begum  ORDER
The petitioners filed this petition to quash the FIR in Crime No.43 of 2019 dated 12.10.2019 on the file of the first respondent herein.
2. The reading of the FIR shows that the marriage between the first petitioner and the second respondent was solemnized on 14.04.2013.
She gave the complaint before the first respondent police alleging that the accused demanded additional dowry and made cruelty on her and her child.

Hence,
the said complaint was registered in Crime No.43 of 2019 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD).No.15624 of 2020 for the offence under Sections 498A, 406 and 506(i) IPC.
Thereafter, they got mutual divorce in O.S.No.60 of 2018 before the Family Court, Madurai.
Even after the legal divorce effected between the parties the FIR is still pending.
Hence, the petitioners filed this petition to quash the said FIR.
3. Pending the quash petition, this Court directed the defacto complainant/2nd respondent to appear before this Court.

The defacto complainant along with her father appeared before this Court and made a submission that she has no objection to quash the proceedings in Crime No.43 of 2019 provided that the first petitioner and his family members shall not interfere their life and also ensure their safety.

She has also produced a written consent letter in this regard before this Court and the same is extracted as follows:

sentences.text: In view of the development between the parties and in order to maintain peace, this Court is inclined to peruse the contents of the FIR.
In the contents of the FIR, it is stated that the accused said to have caused cruelty to the defacto complainant without mentioning any specific date.

In the absence of any specific date and also they got divorce, this Court finds no offence under Sections 498A, 406 and 506(i) IPC is made out. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl.O.P.(MD).No.15624 of 2020

In the said circumstances, this Court is inclined to quash this petition.
6.

Further, consensus had already been arrived at between the parties, no purpose will be served in keeping the First Information Report in Crime No.43 of 2019 pending on the file of the first respondent police.

Hence, this Court is inclined to quash the First Information Report.
7.
In the result, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed and the First Information Report in Crime No.43 of 2019 on the file of the first respondent stands quashed.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
However, this Court directs the petitioner to maintain peace and shall not cause any disturbance to the second respondent and her child.
It is always open to the second respondent to file a complaint if the petitioners would cause any hindrance to her peaceful life in future.
